title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer
talk_summary: The transferable core is not design-specific: define a rigid foundation/spec, generate artifacts programmatically from live data, and use the model as a visual QA checker.

takeaways.technique: Encode a design system as a hard spec before generation
takeaways.what_they_do: They predefine typography scales, colors, components and taglines so the LLM cannot invent random values; they also feed a Figma spec-sheet plugin that annotates spacing/font-size/colors as machine-readable input.

takeaways.technique: Generate deliverables from live data via a tool, not by hand
takeaways.evidence_quote: right now we just pull the latest data. I just asked Devin like, "Hey, I want this room at these days." And then we can just export it
takeaways.numbers: 300+ speakers, 140+ sponsors, 600+ sessions handled by one designer

takeaways.technique: Use the model as a visual/diff QA checker against a known-good list
takeaways.what_they_do: They ask the agent to compare a rendered graphic against the sponsor list and flag missing logos, and report it as effectively perfect on their tests; framed as 'human plus AI = your own QA team'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: could you check if there are any missing logos in this graphic? And the accuracy is 100% based on the test that I do
takeaways.numbers: claims 100% accuracy on their own test

takeaways.technique: Treat exceptions as the real workload; make the pipeline editable
takeaways.what_they_do: They accept that the automated generator handles the happy path and that the human's job is handling exceptions; when a one-off need appears (an edit button on the schedule), they ask the agent to add it to the tool rather than doing it manually.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The real job is handling exceptions... I could just ask Devin, "Hey, can you add me an edit button?" And then it did.

takeaways.technique: Atomic components composed into deliverables (LEGO approach)
takeaways.what_they_do: They build the smallest reusable pieces first and compose them into outputs, so one foundation serves website, emails, flyers, and docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we create the smallest part possible and then combining it into like basically a LEGO pieces and then into a deliverables
